Li metal (Fig. 2b) exhibits a relatively smooth surface, with only a small amount of O detected, indicating slight surface oxidation during sample preparation and transfer. After further oxidation (denoted as LO), inhomogeneously distributed white particles appear on the Li surface and preferentially grow at defect sites, revealing a pronounced defect- sensitive oxidation behavior (Fig. 2c). Such a nonuniform oxide layer not only deteriorates the surface flatness of Li metal, but may also induce localized current-density concentration during subsequent electro­ chemical cycling.
